title: What a program holds
subtitle: A copy that is not a copy, and a call stack

scenes.title: b = a does not copy the list
scenes.narration: In Python, giving a list a second name does not make a second list.

steps.say: After b equals a, both names point at the same list.
So changing b's second item changes a's too.
Copying the list gives b a list of its own, and the two stop sharing.

scenes.title: Each call gets its own frame
scenes.narration: Every call to factorial gets a frame of its own, stacked on the one that called it.

steps.say: Factorial of three needs factorial of two, so a new frame goes on top.
That needs factorial of one, which is the base case.
It returns one, and its frame is gone.
Then the last frame finishes with six.
